previous_evidence.round5_meaning: Near-bulk anchoring kept worst relative error ~6.47e-15, moving anchor 1e9 away gave 0.01120395908 error
previous_evidence.why_this_experiment: Check whether one extreme first sample makes first-item anchor inaccurate; hold exact multiset fixed within each outlier location comparison.

interpretation: Counterexample to the assumption that a distant first sample automatically makes anchored variance inaccurate: in these one-outlier full-population tests, first-sample anchored Welford remained near machine-precision; large outlier dominates total variance, so inlier-scale loss could be masked. This is only an engineering diagnostic.

next_round.experiment: With the exact same seeded inlier-only population (omit the outlier from the target statistic), compare Welford shifted by the prior outlier anchor versus fixed near-bulk anchor under sorted/reversed order, using exact integer-rational inlier variance. This isolates whether the large full-population variance masked anchor error.
next_round.why: One outlier dominates true variance and first-outlier anchoring stayed accurate despite distant anchor; isolate the small-variance inlier regime rather than assume a failure.

scope: CPU-only numerical engineering smoke test, not a public benchmark or research novelty
